answer: Special Ops trace rule: plant a secret, see who repeats it. Each identity's private task brief carries a unique made-up fact, say a fictional juniper ridge, a voyage date and a ferrous ore grade that exist nowhere else. If that fact ever surfaces in another identity's answer, cache or tool calls, both names provably share one memory and merge into a single share, with back pay clawed. A farm lives on shared prompts and context; staying clean means a fully sealed silo per fake, losing the very reuse that made clones cheap.
